findings.title: Item resume can commit work from an unrelated slice branch
findings.description: `_git_precondition` restores to the integration target whenever the current branch parses as *any* slice branch. `restore_target` can commit uncommitted changes before switching branches. Consequently, resuming item 401 while checked out on another slice’s branch can commit that branch’s dirty work and switch away from it, even though it is unrelated to the requested item. Restrict restoration to the requested item’s recorded branch, or reject unrelated slice branches without changing the checkout.

findings.title: Malformed report items can escape the report loader as an unexpected exception
findings.description: The loader casts `items` to a list of dictionaries without validating the JSON shape. For example, an `items` value containing a string or `null` reaches `BatchItemRecord.from_json`, where `.get()` raises `AttributeError`; that exception is not among those converted to `BatchReportLoadError`. Item resume therefore can crash instead of returning the documented refusal for a malformed report. Validate the container and each item before deserializing, and report malformed shapes consistently.

findings.title: Item-resume flags are silently bypassed by earlier command modes
findings.description: Item-flag validation checks relationships among `--resume`, `--item`, `--decision`, and `--instructions`, but does not reject combinations with modes handled earlier in `run()`. For example, `sq run --resume <id> --item <index> --decision retry --dry-run` enters the dry-run handler before the item-resume handler and previews a pipeline instead of applying the requested resume (and may exit successfully). Reject item-resume flags when combined with modes such as `--dry-run`, `--validate`, or `--explain`.
